sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Gloucester Township, NJ?
sections.html:
Most Gloucester Township owners choose between a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash offer, and the fastest route is the one that has the fewest repairs and approvals in the way. The township sits in Camden County, and the Census Bureau estimates its population at 67,085 for July 1, 2025, and it ranked 22nd among New Jersey's 565 municipalities by population in the 2020 census.

Housing here leans toward ownership: 73.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median value is $277,800. That mix of long-held family homes and a steady supply of listings means a house that needs work competes with move-in-ready neighbors, so an as-is cash sale appeals to owners who would rather skip repairs, showings and a lender's timeline.

sections.h2: What is Gloucester Township like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Gloucester Township spans 22.95 square miles of land and includes the communities of Blackwood, Glendora and Grenloch along with Chews Landing, Erial, Glen Oaks, Lambs Terrace and Turkey Foot. It was formed on June 1, 1695, when the area was still part of Gloucester County, and became part of Camden County when that county was created in 1844. Big Timber Creek flows through the township on its way to the Delaware River.

The township borders Hi-Nella, Lindenwold, Magnolia, Pine Hill, Runnemede, Somerdale, Stratford and Winslow Township in Camden County, and Deptford Township and Washington Township in Gloucester County. Camden County College's 320-acre campus in Blackwood took its first students in 1968.

  • Blackwood and Glendora: census-designated places with 2020 populations of 4,622 and 4,784.
  • Erial: an unincorporated community that is home to Timber Creek Regional High School.
  • The Atlantic City Expressway corridor, which passes through the southwest part of the township.

sections.h2: Who handles the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate in Gloucester Township?
sections.html:
In Gloucester Township the fire district that serves your address handles the smoke alarm and carbon monoxide certification, because the township is divided into several fire districts. Fire District No. 4's Bureau of Fire Prevention posts an application for smoke and carbon monoxide certification and takes inspection requests by phone or email.

To learn which district covers your street, open the township's property tax lookup, search by street address and read the Special Taxing Districts line on the property record. A listing of FIRE DISTRICT=F04 means District No. 4. State rules require a certificate before a one-family or two-family house is sold, and it stays valid for six months from the date of issue, so time the inspection close to your closing date.

The district's page says alarm requirements can vary with the property's age and layout and that a failed inspection leads to a list of corrections and a re-inspection. Ask the township construction office whether any other paperwork applies to a resale before you list.

sections.h2: How do Gloucester Township property taxes work at closing?
sections.html:
The township collects tax in quarterly installments due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with the maximum 10-day grace period state law allows. Interest is 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 of a delinquency and 18 percent on the rest, and the tax office adds a 6 percent penalty on a balance above $10,000 left unpaid at year end. Delinquent current-year taxes as of November 11 can be sold at tax sale before December 30, and payments during that period must be made with cash or certified funds.

The tax office notes two standard deductions of $250, one for qualifying seniors and disabled residents and one for veterans. Late tax levy certification pushed the third-quarter 2026 grace period to September 2, 2026, a reminder that bills and dates can shift, so ask the tax collector for a written payoff figure before closing.

To challenge an assessment, file with the Camden County Board of Taxation by 4:00 p.m. on April 1, or May 1 in a town that did a revaluation. The filing fee for an assessment between $150,000 and $500,000 is $25, which covers the township's average residential assessment. Keep paying your taxes while the appeal is pending, because a missed payment can get it dismissed.

sections.h2: What costs and forms come with a Gloucester Township sale?
sections.html:
Selling here follows the state's closing rules, and the largest line items are usually the payoff and the transfer fee. The seller pays the Realty Transfer Fee at recording. On a deal at or below $350,000 the rate is $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 per $500 up to $200,000 and $3.90 per $500 up to $350,000, so a $325,000 sale carries a fee of $1,910, the example the state itself uses.

  • Realty Transfer Fee, set by the state's rate table.
  • Payoff of the mortgage, home equity line or tax lien.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate fee from the fire district.
  • Seller's residency certification (GIT/REP-3) for the deed.

Deeds are recorded with the Camden County Clerk at 520 Market Street in Camden, and the office accepts electronic recording. Sellers who live out of state owe an estimated Gross Income Tax payment of at least 2 percent of the price unless an exemption on the GIT/REP-3 applies.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit matter to Gloucester Township buyers?
sections.html:
Gloucester Township Public Schools serve prekindergarten through eighth grade with eight elementary schools and three middle schools: Glen Landing, Charles W. Lewis and Ann A. Mullen. High school students attend Highland Regional in Blackwood, Timber Creek Regional in Erial or Triton Regional in Runnemede, assigned by home address, all within the Black Horse Pike Regional School District.

In 2010 the township listed 239.44 miles of road, 186.25 of them municipal. The Atlantic City Expressway crosses the southwest corner, Routes 42 and 168 pass through the western part, and County Routes 534 and 544 run through the center and along the northern edge. NJ Transit bus route 400 connects to Philadelphia, with local routes 403 and 459.

sections.h2: What should a landlord know before selling a Gloucester Township rental?
sections.html: The township's downloads page carries a Landlord Identity Registration form, so a rental owner should confirm that registration is current before the house is listed. The median gross rent is $1,592 and about 27 percent of homes are renter-occupied, so tenant-occupied houses are a normal part of the market. The state certificate applies to a lease or change of occupancy as well as a sale.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell in Gloucester Township?
faqs.a: You need the smoke alarm and carbon monoxide certificate, which comes through the fire district that serves your address. Ask the township construction office whether any other resale paperwork applies to your house.

faqs.q: How do I find my fire district in Gloucester Township?
faqs.a: Use the township's property tax lookup, search your street address and read the Special Taxing Districts line. F04 on that line means Fire District No. 4.

faqs.q: When are Gloucester Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Interest accrues at 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent above that, and taxes unpaid after November 11 can go to tax sale.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Gloucester Township?
faqs.a: April 1 at 4:00 p.m., or May 1 where the town has done a revaluation or reassessment. The Camden County Board of Taxation holds hearings at 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood and offers a summary hearing without an appearance.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gloucester Township house that is in foreclosure or has liens?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale price covers the payoff. Ask each lender and the tax collector for written payoff figures, since tax sale charges add fees beyond the posted tax total.
